cause: LiliesStorage used sqlite3.Connection as a transaction context manager in 46 call sites, but sqlite3.Connection.__exit__ commits or rolls back without closing the connection. A long Builder run therefore accumulated database, WAL, and shared-memory file descriptors until the next get_session read surfaced sqlite3.OperationalError: disk I/O error at the clients table. The platform received HTTP 502 and durably failed the assignment as daemon_rejected. Post-run quick_check passed, the database remained readable, and the volume retained 169 GiB free, excluding persistent corruption and capacity exhaustion.

It proves neither the revision-17 permission projection repair under a real oversized request nor customer workflow delivery and remains a failed customer attempt in the project denominator.
retained_fix_route: Use one generic transaction context that always closes its SQLite connection after commit or rollback, replace every storage call site, and verify exact opened/closed parity, exception closure, concurrent live-WAL monitoring, and the complete Lilies regression surface. Do not convert persistent or corrupt-database failures into retries or success. Freeze a child revision only after those checks and fresh read-only review pass.
